synthesis: Six retrieved records from the broader second search, appraised at abstract level; the first, narrower search returned nothing. Against population controls, cardiovascular risk after pneumonia is raised most in the first year (hazard ratio 1.9) and less in years two to five (1.3), and adjustment for earlier cardiovascular disease and frailty shrinks the later excess to about 1.15. Against patients admitted with other infections, the mortality excess is small and concentrated in the first year. Methods work shows the two comparison groups bracket the truth. Care home entry doubles in older adults. Linkage is near complete. No retrieved record supports a ten-year doubling of cardiovascular risk.
gradeRationale: Consistent observational cohorts with serious confounding by frailty and comparison-group choice; estimates shrink with better adjustment. Low certainty that a long-term cardiovascular excess persists beyond the first year.
summary: Six retrieved records appraised after an empty first search; five claims recorded; overall certainty low.
